key_insight: Photovoltaics look energetically strong at the panel level, but their net energy and climate advantage drop sharply once reliable, round-the-clock supply constraints are included.
engineering_relevance: Grid planners must treat firming, storage, backup, and overbuild as first-order design variables because they can dominate the system-level EROI and emissions balance.
method: Benchmark, fleet-equivalent accounting model for wind-PV mixes
Includes component turnover, grids, storage, overbuild, backup, and fuel supply
Compares unfir​med operation with battery, hydrogen, and gas firming options
evidence_signal: The abstract reports EROI falling from 10.7-16.0 unfir​med to 0.7-2.3 for 24h battery balancing, 3.4-7.7 for seasonal hydrogen, and only 1.0-2.6 for gas/LNG backup, with GWP$_{100}$ rising to 80-327 gCO2eq/kWh depending on firming pathway.
watch_item: This is an illustrative accounting benchmark with idealized assumptions, so real deployments with non-unity orientation, siting, curtailment, and delivery factors will perform worse.
paper_title: Photovoltaics beyond the panel: system-level net energy under grid and firming constraints
